name: Nuclear risk
value: No US–Russia treaty limits since 5 Feb
summary: No US–Russia arms limits since New START lapsed; Trump, Xi and Putin meet in Shenzhen on 19 Nov
state: New START expired on 5 Feb with no replacement. Trump, Xi and Putin are due to meet at APEC in Shenzhen on 19 Nov with nuclear weapons reduction on the agenda, though US officials said on 13 Nov they did not expect an agreement and China has rejected trilateral arms control (The National, 17 Nov). Trump said on 16 Nov he may also meet Kim Jong-un. No nuclear test, alert-level change or threatened use was found as of 17 Nov, so Watch holds.
for_you: US and Russian nuclear arsenals have had no treaty limits since 5 Feb. US officials describe the 19 Nov summit as a starting point for talks rather than a deal.
rubric_hit: Arms-control lapse without replacement (New START expired 5 Feb) = Watch; no test or alert change

sources.title: Trump to hold nuclear talks with Xi and Putin, with Kim Jong-un possibly joining

why: Nuclear use anywhere would be a civilisational shock; arms-control treaties are weaker than at any time since the 1960s.
drivers: Threats in active wars, testing, doctrine changes, arms-control collapse, proliferation.

rubric.alert: A nuclear test, changes in deployment/alert levels, or threatened use in an active conflict.
rubric.watch: Explicit threats, unusual exercises, doctrine changes, or arms-control lapses without replacement.
rubric.normal: No explicit nuclear threats or tests; arms-control dialogue active.
